sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatir abhūt karṇo dauryodhane bale akṣauhiṇībhiḥ śiṣṭābhir vṛtaḥ pañcabhir āhave
english: Then Karṇa became the commander of Duryodhana's army, surrounded in battle by the five akṣauhiṇīs that yet remained.

sanskrit: tisras tu pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ camvo bībhatsupālitāḥ hatapravīrabhūyiṣṭhā babhūvuḥ samavasthitāḥ
english: The three divisions of the sons of Pāṇḍu, guarded by Bībhatsu, stood firm in their array, though most of their foremost heroes had been slain.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthaṃ samāsādya pataṃga iva pāvakam pañcatvam agamat sautir dvitīye 'hani dāruṇe
english: Then, having closed with Pārtha as a moth flies into the flame, the son of the charioteer met his dissolution on the second dreadful day.

sanskrit: hate karṇe tu kauravyā nirutsāhā hataujasaḥ akṣauhiṇībhis tisṛbhir madreśaṃ paryavārayan
english: When Karṇa was slain, the Kauravas, dispirited and stripped of vigor, with their three remaining akṣauhiṇīs surrounded the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: hatavāhanabhūyiṣṭhāḥ pāṇḍavās tu yudhiṣṭhiram akṣauhiṇyā nirutsāhāḥ śiṣṭayā paryavārayan
english: The Pāṇḍavas, most of whose mounts had been killed and who too were dispirited, surrounded Yudhiṣṭhira with the single akṣauhiṇī that remained.

sanskrit: avadhīn madrarājānaṃ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tasmiṃs tathārdhadivase karma kṛtvā suduṣkaram
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, king of the Kurus, slew the king of the Madras, accomplishing on that half-day a deed most hard to do.

sanskrit: hate śalye tu śakuniṃ sahadevo mahāmanāḥ āhartāraṃ kales tasya jaghānāmitavikramaḥ
english: When Śalya was slain, the high-minded Sahadeva, of boundless valor, struck down Śakuni, the very kindler of that strife.

sanskrit: nihate śakunau rājā dhārtarāṣṭraḥ sudurmanāḥ apākrāmad gadāpāṇir hatabhūyiṣṭhasainikaḥ
english: When Śakuni was killed, the king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, sore at heart, withdrew, mace in hand, most of his soldiers slain.

sanskrit: tam anvadhāvat saṃkruddho bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān hrade dvaipāyane cāpi salilasthaṃ dadarśa tam
english: The mighty Bhīmasena, filled with wrath, pursued him, and beheld him standing within the waters of the Dvaipāyana lake.

sanskrit: tataḥ śiṣṭena sainyena samantāt parivārya tam upopaviviśur hṛṣṭā hradasthaṃ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Then, surrounding him on every side with the army that remained, the five Pāṇḍavas, exultant, sat down close about him as he stood in the lake.

sanskrit: vigāhya salilaṃ tv āśu vāgbāṇair bhṛśavikṣataḥ utthāya sa gadāpāṇir yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ
english: Plunging swiftly through the water, sorely pierced by their arrows of words, he rose up, mace in hand, and stood ready for battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa nihato rājā dhārtarāṣṭro mahāmṛdhe bhīmasenena vikramya paśyatāṃ pṛthivīkṣitām
english: Then that king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, was slain in the great combat by Bhīmasena's prowess, before the eyes of the rulers of the earth.

sanskrit: tatas tat pāṇḍavaṃ sainyaṃ saṃsuptaṃ śibire niśi nihataṃ droṇaputreṇa pitur vadham amṛṣyatā
english: Thereafter the army of the Pāṇḍavas, asleep at night in its camp, was slaughtered by the son of Droṇa, who could not bear his father's slaying.

sanskrit: hataputrā hatabalā hatamitrā mayā saha yuyudhānadvitīyena pañca śiṣṭāḥ sma pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Their sons slain, their forces slain, their friends slain, the five Pāṇḍavas alone survived, together with me and with Yuyudhāna as a sixth.

sanskrit: sahaiva kṛpabhojābhyāṃ drauṇir yuddhād amucyata yuyutsuś cāpi kauravyo muktaḥ pāṇḍavasaṃśrayāt
english: The son of Droṇa, together with Kṛpa and the Bhoja, escaped from the war; and Yuyutsu the Kaurava too was spared, having taken refuge with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: nihate kauravendre ca sānubandhe suyodhane viduraḥ saṃjayaś caiva dharmarājam upasthitau
english: When Suyodhana, lord of the Kurus, was slain along with all his kin, both Vidura and Saṃjaya came and waited upon the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: evaṃ tad abhavad yuddham ahāny aṣṭādaśa prabho yatra te pṛthivīpālā nihatāḥ svargam āvasan
english: Thus, O lord, did that war last eighteen days, wherein those guardians of the earth, being slain, came to dwell in heaven.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇvatāṃ tu mahārāja kathāṃ tāṃ romaharṣaṇīm duḥkhaharṣaparikleśā vṛṣṇīnām abhavaṃs tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As they listened to that hair-raising tale, O great king, the Vṛṣṇis were then beset by anguish, joy, and torment all at once.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kathayann eva tu tadā vāsudevaḥ pratāpavān mahābhāratayuddhaṃ tat kathānte pitur agrataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the mighty Vāsudeva was recounting that great Bhārata war, there before his father, at the close of his telling—

sanskrit: abhimanyor vadhaṃ vīraḥ so 'tyakrāmata bhārata apriyaṃ vasudevasya mā bhūd iti mahāmanāḥ
english: —the hero, O Bhārata, the high-minded one, passed over the slaying of Abhimanyu, that it might bring no grief to Vasudeva.

sanskrit: mā dauhitravadhaṃ śrutvā vasudevo mahātyayam duḥkhaśokābhisaṃtapto bhaved iti mahāmatiḥ
english: For the wise one thought: let not Vasudeva, hearing of the dread slaying of his daughter's son, be consumed by sorrow and grief.

sanskrit: subhadrā tu tam utkrāntam ātmajasya vadhaṃ raṇe ācakṣva kṛṣṇa saubhadravadham ity apatad bhuvi
english: But Subhadrā, marking that he had passed over the slaying of her son in battle, cried, "Kṛṣṇa, tell of the death of Saubhadra!" and fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: tām apaśyan nipatitāṃ vasudevaḥ kṣitau tadā dṛṣṭvaiva ca papātorvyāṃ so 'pi duḥkhena mūrchitaḥ
english: Vasudeva then saw her fallen upon the earth, and at the very sight he too sank to the ground, swooning with grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa dauhitravadhād duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ vasudevo mahārāja kṛṣṇaṃ vākyam athābravīt
english: Then Vasudeva, O great king, overcome with sorrow and grief at the slaying of his daughter's son, spoke these words to Kṛṣṇa:

sanskrit: nanu tvaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa satyavāg bhuvi viśrutaḥ yad dauhitravadhaṃ me 'dya na khyāpayasi śatruhan
english: "Surely, lotus-eyed one, you are renowned upon earth as a speaker of truth, O slayer of foes—why then do you not tell me today of my grandson's death?

sanskrit: tad bhāgineyanidhanaṃ tattvenācakṣva me vibho sadṛśākṣas tava kathaṃ śatrubhir nihato raṇe
english: Tell me truly, O lord, of the death of your sister's son. How was that boy, whose eyes were like your own, slain by the foe in battle?

sanskrit: durmaraṃ bata vārṣṇeya kāle 'prāpte nṛbhiḥ sadā yatra me hṛdayaṃ duḥkhāc chatadhā na vidīryate
english: Hard indeed it is, O Vārṣṇeya, for men ever to die before their time has come—since my heart for grief does not shatter into a hundred pieces!

sanskrit: kim abravīt tvā saṃgrāme subhadrāṃ mātaraṃ prati māṃ cāpi puṇḍarīkākṣa capalākṣaḥ priyo mama
english: What did he say to you in the battle concerning his mother Subhadrā, and concerning me, O lotus-eyed one—that restless-eyed boy so dear to me?

sanskrit: āhavaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā kaccin na nihataḥ paraiḥ kaccin mukhaṃ na govinda tenājau vikṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: He was not slain by the enemy turning his back upon the fight, was he? Tell me, Govinda, that he never made his face turn away in that combat.

sanskrit: sa hi kṛṣṇa mahātejāḥ ślāghann iva mamāgrataḥ bālabhāvena vijayam ātmano 'kathayat prabhuḥ
english: For that mighty-splendored lordling, O Kṛṣṇa, would boast as it were before me, and in his boyish way would tell of his own victories.

sanskrit: kaccin na vikṛto bālo droṇakarṇakṛpādibhiḥ dharaṇyāṃ nihataḥ śete tan mamācakṣva keśava
english: That the boy was not maimed and laid low upon the earth by Droṇa, Karṇa, Kṛpa and the rest—this tell me, O Keśava.

sanskrit: sa hi droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca rathināṃ varam spardhate sma raṇe nityaṃ duhituḥ putrako mama
english: For my daughter's little son would ever vie in war with Droṇa, with Bhīṣma, and with Karṇa, the foremost of chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhaṃ bahu tadā vilapantaṃ suduḥkhitam pitaraṃ duḥkhitataro govindo vākyam abravīt
english: As his father lamented thus at length, sore stricken, Govinda, more stricken still, spoke these words:

sanskrit: na tena vikṛtaṃ vaktraṃ kṛtaṃ saṃgrāmamūrdhani na pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtaś cāpi saṃgrāmas tena dustaraḥ
english: "He never turned his face away at the forefront of the battle, nor did he wage that grievous fight with his back to the foe.

sanskrit: nihatya pṛthivīpālān sahasraśatasaṃghaśaḥ khedito droṇakarṇābhyāṃ dauḥśāsanivaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Having slain guardians of the earth by the hundred thousand in their hosts, worn down at last by Droṇa and Karṇa, he fell into the power of Duḥśāsana's son.

sanskrit: eko hy ekena satataṃ yudhyamāno yadi prabho na sa śakyeta saṃgrāme nihantum api vajriṇā
english: For so long as he fought one against one, O lord, he could not have been slain in battle even by the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: samāhūte tu saṃgrāme pārthe saṃśaptakais tadā paryavāryata saṃkruddhaiḥ sa droṇādibhir āhave
english: But when Pārtha had been drawn off into combat by the sworn warriors, the boy was hemmed in by Droṇa and the rest, all furious, in that battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatrukṣayaṃ kṛtvā sumahāntaṃ raṇe pituḥ dauhitras tava vārṣṇeya dauḥśāsanivaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Then, having wrought a very great slaughter of his father's foes in battle, your daughter's son, O Vārṣṇeya, fell into the power of Duḥśāsana's son.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ ca sa gataḥ svargaṃ jahi śokaṃ mahāmate na hi vyasanam āsādya sīdante sannarāḥ kva cit
english: Surely he has gone to heaven; cast off your grief, O wise one. Good men, meeting with calamity, never sink down into despair.

sanskrit: droṇakarṇaprabhṛtayo yena pratisamāsitāḥ raṇe mahendrapratimāḥ sa kathaṃ nāpnuyād divam
english: He by whom Droṇa, Karṇa and the rest, peers of great Indra, were met in battle—how should he not attain heaven?

sanskrit: sa śokaṃ jahi durdharṣa mā ca manyuvaśaṃ gamaḥ śastrapūtāṃ hi sa gatiṃ gataḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Cast off your grief, O unassailable one, and do not yield to anguish; for that conqueror of hostile cities has won the goal hallowed by the sword."

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre subhadreyaṃ svasā mama duḥkhārtātho pṛthāṃ prāpya kurarīva nanāda ha
english: But when that hero was slain, this Subhadrā, my sister, stricken with grief, came to Pṛthā and shrieked aloud like an osprey.

sanskrit: draupadīṃ ca samāsādya paryapṛcchata duḥkhitā ārye kva dārakāḥ sarve draṣṭum icchāmi tān aham
english: And drawing near to Draupadī, she asked in her grief: "Noble lady, where are all our boys? I long to look upon them."

sanskrit: asyās tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sarvās tāḥ kuruyoṣitaḥ bhujābhyāṃ parigṛhyaināṃ cukruśuḥ paramārtavat
english: Hearing her words, all those women of the Kurus took her in their arms and wailed in utmost anguish.

sanskrit: uttarāṃ cābravīd bhadrā bhadre bhartā kva te gataḥ kṣipram āgamanaṃ mahyaṃ tasmai tvaṃ vedayasva ha
english: And Bhadrā said to Uttarā: "Gentle one, where has your husband gone? Tell him to come to me quickly."

sanskrit: nanu nāma sa vairāṭi śrutvā mama giraṃ purā bhavanān niṣpataty āśu kasmān nābhyeti te patiḥ
english: "Surely, daughter of Virāṭa, in former days, on hearing my voice, he would rush forth at once from the house. Why does your lord not come to you now?"

sanskrit: abhimanyo kuśalino mātulās te mahārathāḥ kuśalaṃ cābruvan sarve tvāṃ yuyutsum ihāgatam
english: "O Abhimanyu, your uncles, the great chariot-warriors, are well; and all of them have asked after your welfare, you who came here eager for battle."

sanskrit: ācakṣva me 'dya saṃgrāmaṃ yathāpūrvam ariṃdama kasmād eva vilapatīṃ nādyeha pratibhāṣase
english: "Tell me now of the battle as before, O subduer of foes. Why do you not answer me here today as I lament?"

sanskrit: evamādi tu vārṣṇeyyās tad asyāḥ paridevitam śrutvā pṛthā suduḥkhārtā śanair vākyam athābravīt
english: Hearing this and the rest of the lament of the Vṛṣṇi lady, Pṛthā, sore stricken with grief, then slowly spoke these words:

sanskrit: subhadre vāsudevena tathā sātyakinā raṇe pitrā ca pālito bālaḥ sa hataḥ kāladharmaṇā
english: "Subhadrā, the boy who was guarded in battle by Vāsudeva, by Sātyaki, and by his own father, was slain by the law of Time.

sanskrit: īdṛśo martyadharmo 'yaṃ mā śuco yadunandini putro hi tava durdharṣaḥ saṃprāptaḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: Such is the law of mortals; grieve not, O delight of the Yadus. For your unconquerable son has attained the supreme goal.

sanskrit: kule mahati jātāsi kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahātmanām mā śucaś capalākṣaṃ tvaṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇe
english: You are born in a great house of high-souled warriors; grieve not for the restless-eyed boy, O you whose eyes are like the lotus.

sanskrit: uttarāṃ tvam avekṣasva garbhiṇīṃ mā śucaḥ śubhe putram eṣā hi tasyāśu janayiṣyati bhāminī
english: Look to Uttarā, who is with child; grieve not, O lovely one. For this fair lady will soon bring forth his son."

sanskrit: evam āśvāsayitvaināṃ kuntī yadukulodvaha vihāya śokaṃ durdharṣaṃ śrāddham asya hy akalpayat
english: Having thus comforted her, O upholder of the Yadu line, Kuntī cast off her hard-to-bear grief and made ready his funeral rites.

sanskrit: samanujñāpya dharmajñā rājānaṃ bhīmam eva ca yamau yamopamau caiva dadau dānāny anekaśaḥ
english: With the leave of the king, of Bhīma too, and of the twins who were the peers of Yama, the knower of dharma bestowed gifts in great abundance.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradāya bahvīr gā brāhmaṇebhyo yadūdvaha samahṛṣyata vārṣṇeyī vairāṭīṃ cābravīd idam
english: Then, having given many cows to the brāhmaṇas, O upholder of the Yadus, the Vṛṣṇi lady grew calmer and said this to the daughter of Virāṭa:

sanskrit: vairāṭi neha saṃtāpas tvayā kāryo yaśasvini bhartāraṃ prati suśroṇi garbhasthaṃ rakṣa me śiśum
english: "Daughter of Virāṭa, you must not grieve here for your husband, O glorious one. Fair-hipped lady, guard for me the child within your womb."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ kuntī virarāma mahādyute tām anujñāpya caivemāṃ subhadrāṃ samupānayam
english: Having spoken thus, O most resplendent one, Kuntī fell silent; and taking leave of her, I brought this Subhadrā away.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa nidhanaṃ prāpto dauhitras tava mādhava saṃtāpaṃ jahi durdharṣa mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Thus did your daughter's son meet his end, O Mādhava. Cast off your anguish, O unassailable one, and set not your mind upon grief."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā tu putrasya vacaḥ śūrātmajas tadā vihāya śokaṃ dharmātmā dadau śrāddham anuttamam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing these words of his son, the righteous son of Śūra then cast off his grief and performed a funeral rite beyond compare.

sanskrit: tathaiva vāsudevo 'pi svasrīyasya mahātmanaḥ dayitasya pitur nityam akarod aurdhvadehikam
english: Vāsudeva likewise, for the dear and high-souled son of his sister, duly performed the rites for the departed.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ śatasahasrāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ mahābhujaḥ vidhivad bhojayām āsa bhojyaṃ sarvaguṇānvitam
english: The mighty-armed one feasted sixty hundred-thousands of brāhmaṇas, after due rule, with food endowed with every excellence.

sanskrit: ācchādya ca mahābāhur dhanatṛṣṇām apānudat brāhmaṇānāṃ tadā kṛṣṇas tad abhūd romaharṣaṇam
english: And the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, having clothed the brāhmaṇas, drove away their thirst for wealth; and that was a thing to make the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ caiva gāś caiva śayanācchādanaṃ tathā dīyamānaṃ tadā viprāḥ prabhūtam iti cābruvan
english: Gold, cows, beds and coverings—as these were being given, the brāhmaṇas then cried out, "It is enough, it is more than enough!"

sanskrit: vāsudevo 'tha dāśārho baladevaḥ sasātyakiḥ abhimanyos tadā śrāddham akurvan satyakas tadā atīva duḥkhasaṃtaptā na śamaṃ copalebhire
english: Then Vāsudeva the Dāśārha, Baladeva with Sātyaki, and Satyaka performed the funeral rite of Abhimanyu; sorely consumed with grief, they could find no peace.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā vīrā nagare nāgasāhvaye nopagacchanti vai śāntim abhimanyuvinākṛtāḥ
english: In the same way the heroic Pāṇḍavas, in the city named for the elephant, found no peace, bereft as they were of Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: subahūni ca rājendra divasāni virāṭajā nābhuṅkta patiśokārtā tad abhūt karuṇaṃ mahat kukṣistha eva tasyāstu sa garbhaḥ saṃpralīyata
english: And for very many days, O lord of kings, the daughter of Virāṭa, stricken with grief for her husband, took no food—a most piteous thing—and the child within her womb began to fade away.

sanskrit: ājagāma tato vyāso jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā āgamya cābravīd dhīmān pṛthāṃ pṛthulalocanām uttarāṃ ca mahātejāḥ śokaḥ saṃtyajyatām ayam
english: Then Vyāsa came, having known it by his divine sight; and arriving, the wise and mighty-splendored one said to large-eyed Pṛthā and to Uttarā: "Let this grief be cast away.

sanskrit: janiṣyati mahātejāḥ putras tava yaśasvini prabhāvād vāsudevasya mama vyāharaṇād api pāṇḍavānām ayaṃ cānte pālayiṣyati medinīm
english: A son of great splendor shall be born to you, O glorious one, through the power of Vāsudeva and through the word I speak as well; and at the last he shall rule the earth on behalf of the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaṃ ca saṃprekṣya dharmarājasya paśyataḥ vyāso vākyam uvācedaṃ harṣayann iva bhārata
english: And looking upon Dhanaṃjaya, while the King of Righteousness watched, Vyāsa spoke these words, as though to gladden them, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: pautras tava mahābāho janiṣyati mahāmanāḥ pṛthvīṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ pālayiṣyati caiva ha
english: "A high-minded grandson shall be born to you, O mighty-armed one, and he shall rule the earth to the very bounds of the sea.

sanskrit: tasmāc chokaṃ kuruśreṣṭha jahi tvam arikarśana vicāryam atra na hi te satyam etad bhaviṣyati
english: Therefore cast off your grief, O best of Kurus, O harrower of foes. There is no room for doubt in this: truly it shall come to pass for you.

sanskrit: yac cāpi vṛṣṇivīreṇa kṛṣṇena kurunandana puroktaṃ tat tathā bhāvi mā te 'trāstu vicāraṇā
english: And what was foretold before by the Vṛṣṇi hero Kṛṣṇa, O delight of the Kurus, shall so come to be; let there be no doubting of it in your mind.

sanskrit: vibudhānāṃ gato lokān akṣayān ātmanirjitān na sa śocyas tvayā tāta na cānyaiḥ kurubhis tathā
english: He has gone to the imperishable worlds of the gods, won by his own deeds. He is not to be mourned by you, dear child, nor by the other Kurus either."

sanskrit: evaṃ pitāmahenokto dharmātmā sa dhanaṃjayaḥ tyaktvā śokaṃ mahārāja hṛṣṭarūpo 'bhavat tadā
english: Thus addressed by his grandsire, the righteous Dhanaṃjaya cast off his grief, O great king, and grew glad of heart.

sanskrit: pitāpi tava dharmajña garbhe tasmin mahāmate avardhata yathākālaṃ śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī
english: And your father too, O knower of dharma, O great-minded one, grew within that womb in due season, as the moon waxes in the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcodayām āsa vyāso dharmātmajaṃ nṛpam aśvamedhaṃ prati tadā tataḥ so 'ntarhito 'bhavat
english: Then Vyāsa urged the king, the son of Dharma, to undertake the horse-sacrifice; and thereupon he vanished from sight.

sanskrit: dharmarājo 'pi medhāvī śrutvā vyāsasya tad vacaḥ vittopanayane tāta cakāra gamane matim
english: And the wise King of Righteousness, hearing those words of Vyāsa, set his mind, dear child, upon a journey to bring back wealth.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca śrutvaitad vacanaṃ brahman vyāsenoktaṃ mahātmanā aśvamedhaṃ prati tadā kiṃ nṛpaḥ pracakāra ha
english: Janamejaya said: O brāhmaṇa, having heard these words spoken by the high-souled Vyāsa concerning the horse-sacrifice, what then did the king do?

sanskrit: ratnaṃ ca yan maruttena nihitaṃ pṛthivītale tad avāpa kathaṃ ceti tan me brūhi dvijottama
english: And the treasure that was laid by Marutta beneath the surface of the earth—how did he come to win it? Tell me that, O best of the twice-born.
